correctness.rationale: Positive diagonal rescaling to (1,1) preserves the nonzero vector-monomial slots. The zero value and full zero Jacobian leave only the three homogeneous Taylor terms. Any two of the six coefficient rows are independent, so two vanishing slots force both output components to be multiples of the same real homogeneous quadratic. A nondefinite such quadratic has a real zero line (or is identically zero). For a definite one, after choosing its sign, the x², y² and constant slots are nonzero. If the mixed coefficient vanishes, both linear coefficients are nonzero; if it does not, vanishing of both linear coefficients would make the form a multiple of (u−v)². Thus at most four slots cannot give an isolated positive equilibrium. Counting distinct aggregate support slots separately from directed reactions is correct. Direct stoichiometric expansion gives ((x−1)²,(y−1)²) for the stated five positive-rate reactions, so the witness is isolated with full zero Jacobian. This is an analytic check of the universal statement and witness, not a general finite enumeration or a claim for a nonzero nilpotent Jacobian.
